Subject: Hosted access profiles and rate cap clarification

Hi Samira —

Thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment on scope for a Hosted evaluation (so you can compare Hosted vs Dedicated / Private):

- Objective: validate production latency and per-token cost for FinPay’s fraud-scoring pipeline (short instructions + 256 token reply), and confirm secure onboarding for PII-containing prompts.
- Suggested Hosted evaluation surface: one standard text-completion endpoint (llama-3-70b equivalent), one streaming chat endpoint for low-latency scoring, and an embeddings endpoint for your vector index.
- Rate cap ask from your side today: 1,000 concurrent requests peak, typical steady-state 250 rps, median request size ~120 tokens.

What we’ll provide for the Hosted evaluation:
- Sandbox API keys (isolated project, logs retained for 30 days)
- Default rate caps: 500 rps / 5k concurrent tokens across the project (we can raise for the pilot with a short request)
- Recommended warm-up: 48–72 hour ramp with synthetic traffic (we provide a small harness)
- Security: TLS, customer-managed KMS option for Dedicated/Private only (we can share SOC2 artifacts for Hosted)

Attached is the latest ratecard_v2.xlsx and a short SOW_outline.docx draft that outlines responsibilities for the pilot.

Next steps I recommend:
1) You confirm which endpoints you want in the sandbox (completion/chat/embeddings) — reply by EOD Monday.
2) I’ll provision sandbox keys + a temp rate increase request and share the test endpoints.
3) Schedule a 30-min warm-up coordination call with our infra team (Grace) to align ramp windows.

If you need a Dedicated capacity estimate instead, we can run quick throughput checks during the sandbox and produce an apples-to-apples cost/latency comparison.

Thanks,
Sean

1) Your default rate caps show 500 rps / 5k concurrent tokens — can you explain how tokens-concurrency maps to our 1,000 concurrent requests peak? Our requests are small (avg 120 tokens), but we expect bursty traffic during settlement windows.
2) What are the per-minute and per-day quota primitives (we want to avoid sudden blocking during batch runs)?

4) Can the streaming chat endpoint keep <75ms p99 on our median payload size at 250 rps? If not, what fallback behavior do you recommend?

If you can answer these I’ll confirm endpoints. Also looping in our infra lead for scheduling: platform@finpay.io.

Hi Samira — quick answers inline to your questions: 

1) Tokens concurrency mapping: our system tracks both request concurrency and active token concurrency. Rough rule-of-thumb: for 120-token requests, 1,000 concurrent requests ~= 120k concurrent tokens. Our default project cap (5k concurrent tokens) is conservative for early sandboxes. For your expected peak we would submit a temporary rate raise to Hosted ops (we handle transient increases for evaluations). For the pilot I suggest we set an evaluation cap at 150k tokens concurrency (configured for your sandbox project).

2) Quotas: we support per-minute, hourly and daily quotas. For the sandbox I’ll set: 150k concurrent token cap, 18k requests/minute burst window, 6M tokens/day. Those are configurable and we can lock them before the ramp.

3) Logs: yes — sandbox projects get segregated logging and an audit stream you can pull into your Splunk/Datadog. Hosted retains sandbox logs for 30 days by default; if you need longer retention we can add a short-term export during the PoC or discuss a Dedicated plan.

4) p99 latency: streaming chat at 250 rps with your median payload is achievable if request fanout is low (single model route). If you need sub-75ms p99 we recommend: smaller sequence length limit (truncate prompts to 128 tokens), reserve a dedicated model shard for the pilot (we can do this as an add-on), and enable continuous batching with reduced batch windows. If after warm-up your p99 still misses target we’ll propose a Dedicated capacity estimate.

Next actions I’ll take today: provision sandbox project with temporary caps and send keys + endpoint list; upload a short traffic harness to the Drive link below you can run. Grace — can you pick two 30-min slots for the warm-up call (Wed/Thu morning PT)?

Sean
